sections.content: How many people are "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out"?

9,250 people

were counted on the census as "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out mark out metal for machining and fit, assemble and repair machine and press tools, dies, jigs, fixtures and other tools.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" there were more men than women (97.2% compared with 2.8%).

This means "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 97.2% and women made up 2.8% of "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" included:

  • elementary construction occupations (other)
  • security system installers and repairers
  • metal working production and maintenance fitters

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out", 14.8% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" was 16 to 19 years.

We can look at who worked as "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

There is a higher number of men than women with this occupation across all age groups. The age profile for men and women is shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "tool makers, tool fitters and markers-out", 8.8% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (90.9% compared with 9.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.8%) than self-employed (6.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the West Midlands. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the same region of the West Midlands.
